input_signals.name: R&D Cash Conversion Trend
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(MA(RATIO(LAG(xrd, 1), LAG(at, 1)), 3)), RANK(TREND(RATIO(oancf, at), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Sustained lagged R&D intensity predicts higher returns when operating cash profitability is improving.
input_signals.reasoning: Separate scaling and ranking prevent small R&D denominators from generating extreme inverse-intensity observations. The bottleneck construction requires both meaningful prior research commitment and evidence of improving cash conversion, so neither channel can independently produce a high score.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ma( ratio( lag( xrd, 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 3 ) ), rank( trend( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Knowledge-Capital Cash Return
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(LAG(at, 1), LAG(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), 1))), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms generating high sustained operating cash flow relative to their combined conventional and accumulated research capital earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Lagged cumulative R&D augments the invested-capital base rather than serving as a small standalone denominator, avoiding an inverse-R&D-intensity signal. This directly measures cash productivity after capitalizing research and does not multiply separate R&D-intensity and profitability anomalies.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( ma( oancf, 3 ), add( lag( at, 1 ), lag( ts_sum( xrd, 5 ), 1 ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Research-Earnings Joint Floor
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(xrd, sale), 3)), RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ib, at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistently high R&D intensity predicts higher returns when the firm also maintains a positive and durable earnings-profitability floor.
input_signals.reasoning: The signal replaces noisy research peaks and leverage conditioning with a positive ex-ante durability mechanism: sustained innovation backed by earnings resilience. Three-period minima require both channels to survive adverse years, while the continuous bottleneck avoids a degenerate conditional mass and improves coverage relative to longer windows.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ts_min( ratio( xrd, sale ), 3 ) ), rank( ts_min( ratio( ib, at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D-Adjusted Cash Return
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(MA(ADD(oancf, xrd), 3), ADD(LAG(at, 1), LAG(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), 1))), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms generating high pre-R&D operating cash flow relative to their combined physical and accumulated research capital earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The successful knowledge-capital return signal subtracts current R&D through operating cash flow while also capitalizing prior R&D, potentially penalizing research twice. Adding current R&D back estimates pre-investment cash generation, while the augmented capital denominator preserves a direct productivity measure rather than a composite of standalone anomalies.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( ma( add( oancf, xrd ), 3 ), add( lag( at, 1 ), lag( ts_sum( xrd, 5 ), 1 ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: R&D-Adjusted Cash Margin Floor
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(oancf, xrd), sale), 3), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms maintaining a high pre-R&D operating cash margin through adverse periods earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding R&D back to operating cash flow estimates cash generation before discretionary research investment, while the historical minimum requires recurring operating support. This replaces the portfolio-weak rank bottleneck and noisy volatility constructions with a direct downside productivity measure that should retain better coverage than a five-period knowledge stock.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ts_min( ratio( add( oancf, xrd ), sale ), 3 ), 1 )

input_signals.name: R&D-Adjusted Earnings Margin Floor
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ib, xrd), sale), 3), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms maintaining a high earnings margin after reversing immediate R&D expensing earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: R&D is observed and enters directly inside the earnings measure, so the signal cannot collapse into ordinary profitability for a broad zero-imputed population. The downside floor tests whether research-adjusted earnings remain durable through weak periods rather than combining standalone R&D intensity and profitability ranks.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ts_min( ratio( add( ib, xrd ), sale ), 3 ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Earned Funding of Knowledge Capital
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(re, ADD(at, TS_SUM(xrd, 3))), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with substantial cumulative retained earnings relative to their combined reported and research-capital base earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Accumulated R&D enters only as an additional capital requirement, so it cannot mechanically pull negative-retained-earnings firms toward one. The ratio asks whether earned capital is sufficient relative to the knowledge-intensive asset base, producing a monotone funding-quality measure rather than blending raw R&D intensity with RE/AT.

input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( re, add( at, ts_sum( xrd, 3 ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: R&D-Normalized Cash Profitability

input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with strong operating cash profitability after normalizing R&D spending to its recent average earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: When current R&D is below its recent norm, the saved expenditure is removed from cash flow; when R&D is unusually high, the excess investment is added back. This neutralizes the mechanical cash-flow effect of R&D changes rather than betting against cash profitability or repackaging the documented R&D-change anomaly.

input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose cumulative pre-R&D cash generation covers their prior long-horizon research capital earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Three-year pre-R&D cash generation represents resources produced by the business, while the lagged five-year research stock represents knowledge investment awaiting payback. Subtracting the stock before scaling by assets avoids a small R&D denominator and tests realized recovery of prior innovation spending.

input_signals.hypothesis: Firms generating high cash returns on accumulated knowledge capital after normalizing current R&D to its prior three-period average earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The lagged R&D benchmark prevents the normalization adjustment from canceling when cash flow is smoothed over the same window. Cash flow is reduced for temporary R&D cuts and increased for spending above the established benchmark before productivity is measured against the knowledge-capital base.

input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with a high downside floor and a narrow historical range in R&D-adjusted cash margins earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The floor and range are measured in the same cash-margin units, eliminating the scale mismatch between an indicator count and a time-series rank. input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with positive operating cash generation economically matched to sustained R&D spending earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Both bounded shares use the same resource base, so the product is high only when meaningful research spending and positive internal cash generation coexist in balanced proportions. input_signals.hypothesis: Firms emphasizing internally developed research capital over acquired goodwill earn higher returns when supported by durable pre-R&D cash margins.
input_signals.reasoning: The bounded intangible-composition ratio distinguishes organic capability building from acquisition-generated balance-sheet intangibles without simply adding their carrying values. The cash-floor condition tests whether an organic innovation strategy is accompanied by recurring operating economics rather than unproductive research intensity.

input_signals.name: Knowledge Stock Cash Match
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(oancf, xrd), 3), ADD(ABS(TS_SUM(ADD(oancf, xrd), 3)), LAG(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), 1))), RATIO(LAG(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), 1), ADD(ABS(TS_SUM(ADD(oancf, xrd), 3)), LAG(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), 1)))), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose accumulated research capital is matched by commensurate positive pre-R&D cash generation earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The two bounded shares give cumulative cash generation and the lagged knowledge stock equal economic influence, preventing either from numerically swamping the other. Unlike a lookback change to cash return on assets, this tests a stock-output matching mechanism: research capital must be both substantial and supported by realized operating resources.

input_signals.hypothesis: Firms earn lower subsequent returns when accumulated research capital exceeds recent pre-R&D cash-generation capacity.
input_signals.reasoning: The indicator activates the signal only when the knowledge stock actually exceeds cumulative cash capacity, creating the economic asymmetry absent from the prior sign-flipped payback measure. input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high goodwill exposure and short-term debt exceeding downside operating cash capacity earn lower subsequent returns.
